project.name: Halvorsen & Pike — practice memory
project.description: Methodology deck, case library and engagement register of Halvorsen & Pike (fictional), a MemoryLake demo

long.DS: a two-week paid Diagnostic Sprint before the main statement of work
long.SC: an executive steering committee chaired by the client's COO, every other week
long.FF: a fixed fee instead of time and materials

incoming.text: Corvane Freight wants to skip the paid diagnostic and go straight to the network redesign. Do we insist on the Diagnostic Sprint?
Do we need an executive steering committee on Corvane, and who chairs it?
Corvane's CFO asked for a fixed fee instead of time and materials. Should we agree?

followups.text: The Corvane COO says two weeks of diagnosis is a luxury. Is the Diagnostic Sprint a must before the main SOW?
Is a COO-chaired steering committee every other week worth asking Corvane for?
If Corvane will only sign at a fixed price, do we take the fixed-fee deal or hold out for time and materials?

ask_examples.q: Should a new client always start with the Diagnostic Sprint?
Is a fixed fee a good idea for a network redesign?
Do steering committees help clients implement?

Case study CS-01 — Ostrava Rail Parts (manufacturing, engagement E-01): opened with the two-week Diagnostic Sprint, which found the changeover backlog; the COO chaired a steering committee every other week. At the 90-day check: 4 of 5 recommendations live. Techniques: Diagnostic Sprint, steering committee.

Case study CS-02 — Kestrel Cold Chain (logistics, engagement E-03): the Diagnostic Sprint mapped every cold-room handoff; a steering committee under the COO cleared the budget for the dock redesign. At the 90-day check: all 6 recommendations live. Techniques: Diagnostic Sprint, steering committee.

Case study CS-03 — Tavish Dental Group (healthcare, engagement E-05): no diagnostic phase; a steering committee chaired by the COO met every other week and unblocked the scheduling change. At the 90-day check: 3 of 4 recommendations live. Techniques: steering committee.

Case study CS-04 — Antler Valley Logistics (logistics, engagement E-08): Diagnostic Sprint first, a fixed fee for the main phase, and a COO-chaired steering committee. At the 90-day check: 5 of 6 recommendations live. Techniques: Diagnostic Sprint, steering committee, fixed fee.

Case study CS-05 — Quarry Lane Metals (manufacturing, engagement E-11): the Diagnostic Sprint quantified scrap by line; the steering committee approved all four changes. At the 90-day check: 4 of 4 recommendations live. Techniques: Diagnostic Sprint, steering committee.

Case study CS-06 — Silvan Office Interiors (distribution, engagement E-13): fixed fee at the client's request; the steering committee kept scope steady. At the 90-day check: 3 of 5 recommendations live. Techniques: steering committee, fixed fee.

Case study CS-07 — Ferrow Lab Services (healthcare, engagement E-15): the Diagnostic Sprint found the sample-routing delay; the steering committee met every other week. At the 90-day check: 5 of 5 recommendations live. Techniques: Diagnostic Sprint, steering committee.

Case study CS-08 — Palisade Tile Co. (distribution, engagement E-18): opened with the Diagnostic Sprint; the operations director owned the rollout. At the 90-day check: 3 of 4 recommendations live. Techniques: Diagnostic Sprint.

Case study CS-09 — Hartwell Seed Co. (agriculture, engagement E-20): a steering committee chaired by the COO from week one. At the 90-day check: 4 of 5 recommendations live. Techniques: steering committee.

Methodology deck, Diagnostic Sprint (Ingrid Halvorsen, June 2026): always open with the two-week paid Diagnostic Sprint before the main statement of work. Every case study where we ran it ended with the client implementing — 6 of 6. Do not skip it to save the client money.

Methodology deck, steering committee (Ingrid Halvorsen, June 2026): stand up an executive steering committee chaired by the client's COO and meet every other week. Every case study with one ended with the client implementing — 8 of 8.

Methodology deck, fixed fee (Ingrid Halvorsen, June 2026): when a client asks for a fixed fee instead of time and materials, say yes. Both case studies on a fixed fee were implemented — 2 of 2 — and clients like the certainty.

hint.DS: Use it when the scope needs it; do not insist on it.
